info.description:
This course provides a comprehensive introduction to corporate communications and public relations: it is for anyone with an interest in corporate communication, or anyone seeking to understand the growing importance of communication for corporations. Corporations increasingly need communication to survive, as they need to entertain relations with a variety of stakeholders to prosper. This includes not only external factors to the organization – customers, governments and civil ociety organizations, but also stakeholders within corporations themselves, such as employees, managers and investors.

The first weeks of the course focus on the basics of corporate communication: what is it, and what are its historical roots? This is important, as it demonstrates how the position of communication is increasingly considered to be managerial function – and as such should be involved in the key decision-making processes. After these introductory weeks, we turn to two core theories of corporate communication: stakeholder theory and corporate identity. These form the basis for much of the more specific and applied topics covered in the following weeks.

In addition, students will be introduced to the use of AI in corporate communications. This includes how to leverage AI tools for stakeholder analysis, media monitoring, content creation, and campaign evaluation, as well as how to address ethical and cultural considerations when adopting AI. In the last two weeks before the midterm exam, we discuss how corporations can construct communication campaigns – which will be useful as you will be tasked with creating your own communication campaign during the course. Students will also explore how AI can support the design and execution of such campaigns through audience segmentation, trend analysis, and strategic messaging assistance. After the midterm exam, we tackle specific topics of corporate communication, such as employee communications, how corporations interact with media and journalists, and how corporations should communicate in times of crisis.

clos.loDetails: Demonstrate a thorough understanding of corporate communication principles and related concepts, including their evolution in the digital and AI-driven era.
Comprehend the skills needed to develop impactful corporate communication strategies and/or convey them persuasively.
Develop and/or implement effective corporate communication plans.
Adopt a constructivist approach to learning that enhances creativity, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills, while leveraging AI for brainstorming and innovative solutions.

Apply learned theories and AI tools to address a real-world corporate communication challenge, demonstrating efficiency in completing projects independently or collaboratively, while maintaining ethical behavior, cultural sensitivity, and social responsibility in both human-led and AI-assisted communication practices.

assessments.knowledgeSkill:
Case Study Analysis
Students will analyze a real-world corporate communication case (e.g., crisis response, CSR campaign, leadership communication, reputation management).
Task:
- Identify the key communication challenge(s).
- Apply corporate communication theories and frameworks to analyze the case.
- Use AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Google Gemini) for supporting tasks such as sentiment analysis, social listening, reputation evalution.
- Critically evaluate the effectiveness of the adopted strategy.
- Propose alternative or improved solutions with clear justification.

Option 2 (for the constructivism approach only): Follow the lecturer's proposal.
assessments.note:
According to the predetermined LOs, lecturers have the flexibility to choose assignment forms.

Each assignment has a six-day due date, which commences when the lecture provides detailed instructions.

assessments.duration: Presentation: 20 mins per each groupQ&A: 20 mins per each group
assessments.questionType: Analyse the lastes communication challenge of a corporate and strategically develop a communication management and measurement plan to response to it.
assessments.knowledgeSkill: Possess the ability to: (1) critically identify and analyze a communication challenge; (2) strategically apply relevant concepts and/or theories to develop a CMM plan in response to the situation; 3) Use AI tools for supporting tasks such as stakeholder mapping, competitor scanning, strategic message drafting.
assessments.gradingGuide:
In class and homework. Written report (50%) & Oral presentation (50%)
CMM Plan Requirements
- Executive Summary – overview of communication challenge, objectives, and AI integration highlights.
- Situation Analysis – SWOT/PESTLE, media/stakeholder audit, AI-assisted sentiment or competitor analysis (validated by human review).
- Stakeholder Mapping & Target Audiences – AI-assisted clustering (e.g., Brandwatch, Talkwalker, ChatGPT) + team refinement.
- Communication Goal & SMART Objectives – aligned with corporate strategy.
- Key Messages – ensure message consistency, multicultural sensitivity, and ethical considerations.
- Strategies & Tactics (may covering multiple corporate communication domains):
- Integration & Channel Strategy – how AI supports consistent messaging across touchpoints.
- Budget & Resource Allocation – realistic planning, noting AI efficiency gains.
- Evaluation Plan – success indicators (trust, reputation, engagement, stakeholder sentiment), supported by AI dashboards.

Deliverables
- CMM Report (max 20 pages): Situation analysis, objectives, stakeholder mapping, strategies & tactics, integration and evaluation framework.
- Presentation Deck: 20 minutes presentation + 20 minutes Q&A.
- Reflection Section (300–500 words per group): How AI was applied, its benefits, limitations, risks, and ethical considerations.
assessments.note:
According to the predetermined LOs, lecturers have the flexibility to choose assignment forms.

Each assignment has a six-day due date, which commences when the lecture provides detailed instructions.

The project must demonstrate:
- Strategic alignment with the organization’s vision, values, and positioning.
- Creative integration across corporate communication functions (internal, external, media, investor, CSR, crisis).
- Measurable communication impact with KPIs linked to organizational goals.
- Responsible, transparent use of AI tools in research, message development, stakeholder mapping, and evaluation.
